# Paragraph page breaks in unlinked text boxes

Original XML constructed by `tools/textbox_page_break_before_fixture.py` using
python-docx and the repository's original shape helper. No user-template content
or external artwork is included. The reference application exported
`native-verified.pdf` from the schema-valid `control.docx`. The recorder
`tools/record_textbox_page_break_before.py` stores source/PDF SHA-256 hashes,
native text origins and red glyph bounds/bands, without consulting the engine.

Seven pages compare no pageBreakBefore, direct first/middle/last/all paragraphs,
inherited true, and direct false overriding inherited true. Every case displays
Alpha, Beta and Gamma at identical positions inside the same unlinked frame.
The reference application ignores the paragraph page-break property here. This is a text-frame
exception to the general page-start rule in ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.23.
No explicit text-frame exception is stated in that clause. Linked text boxes,
run-level page/column breaks and page breaks inside table cells remain guarded.

The source declarations remain intact. Only text-frame layout suppresses the
resolved pageBreakBefore property. Seven native/browser frame pairs were
visually inspected; all 35 measured text lines match within 0.053pt horizontally
and 0.049pt vertically. Browser tests check every red glyph row band and bounds,
body edits, unrelated-part preservation, no-edit/exact undo and export/reopen.

`oversized-body.docx`, generated by `tools/oversized_body_preview_fixture.py`,
contains two original 650pt Arial letters with a paragraph break before B.
The reference application's `oversized-native.pdf` has two pages. The editor retains the two-page
formatted read-only preview when editing layout rejects the oversized lines;
downloads preserve the original package. This control does not establish full
oversized-line editing or all native overflow placement rules. Those remain work
in progress. No font assets are redistributed.
